_meta.note: Shipped with the add-in. Do not edit here; add overrides in user.json via add_lesson.

instructions.intro: VB6MCP usage notes (read before calling tools):
rules: Compile before you trust: use build (offline /make) or make_project (in-IDE) and check the result; a passing lint is not a compile.
validate_code BEFORE writing: it runs INSIDE the add-in (a live IDE is required - it is NOT an offline check), it is not the VB6 compiler, and it reports a stable ruleId + line.
Editing is IDE-side: edit_by_anchor/apply_edits change the in-memory CodeModule; verify() reports IDE vs DISK, it does not save.
make_project pins the build target and deletes the stale output first, which is what keeps VB6's Make/overwrite dialogs away.
The project must be closed before rebuilding THIS add-in DLL, otherwise /make cannot overwrite the loaded DLL.
Long tool results are JSON on one line; parse them, do not eyeball truncated text.

lessons.scenario: MCP client is configured but registers ZERO tools
lessons.trap: The server answers initialize with a protocolVersion the official client does not list in its SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS. The client rejects the handshake and registers no tools, while the server looks perfectly healthy.
lessons.do: Echo the version the client asked for when it is one we implement; otherwise answer with the latest official version. Never advertise a custom/stateless version here.

lessons.scenario: MCP responses silently dropped
lessons.trap: A _meta key on the JSON-RPC envelope (same level as jsonrpc/id/result). The official SDK JSONRPCMessageSchema is strict, treats it as 'Unrecognized key' and DISCARDS the whole response.
lessons.do: Put _meta inside result only. Keep the envelope to exactly jsonrpc/id/result or jsonrpc/id/error.

lessons.scenario: tools/list rejected by a strict client
lessons.trap: nextCursor emitted as null (must be a string or omitted), or non-official fields such as ttlMs / cacheScope.
lessons.do: Return exactly {tools:[...]}. Omit nextCursor instead of sending null.

lessons.scenario: Believing a protocol change works because it compiles and returns HTTP 200
lessons.trap: The tool list is only populated after a successful strict-schema handshake; compile success and HTTP 200 prove nothing about registration.
lessons.do: Connect with the real client and confirm the tools actually appear; use tools/mcp_strict_audit.py for the schema half.

lessons.scenario: Rebuilding the VB6MCP add-in DLL
lessons.trap: The running VB6 IDE has VB6MCP.dll loaded (image lock), so /make cannot overwrite it - build.bat can still exit 0 while the DLL is unchanged.
lessons.do: Close the IDE first, then run build.bat, then confirm the DLL timestamp/size actually changed.

lessons.scenario: make_project or File>Make pops a modal dialog
lessons.trap: An empty BuildFileName opens the Make Project file dialog; an existing output opens Confirm Save As (a DirectUI dialog that ignores BM_CLICK/WM_COMMAND). The add-in is blocked inside the modal call and cannot click its own dialog.
lessons.do: Pin BuildFileName and delete the stale output before compiling. For a manual File>Make on an open project, expect the per-session dialog; dismiss it from another process (tools/dialog_watch.py) only as a fallback.

lessons.scenario: Reading a nested JSON object in VB6
lessons.trap: p = obj.Item("params") where the item is an object raises error 450; under On Error Resume Next it is silently swallowed and p stays Empty, so the value is never read.
lessons.do: Use Set, or JsonLib.JsonGet (which does Set internally).

lessons.scenario: Rewriting a shorter file
lessons.trap: Open ... For Binary Access Write does NOT truncate, so the old tail survives and the file is corrupted.
lessons.do: Kill the target path first, then write.

lessons.scenario: Comparing a prefix
lessons.trap: Left$(s, n) returns the whole string when n exceeds its length, so comparing against a longer literal silently never matches (Left$(L,5)="loop" never matches "loop while").
lessons.do: Use the exact length of the literal you are matching.

lessons.scenario: stdio MCP bridge on Chinese Windows
lessons.trap: Text-mode stdio uses the console code page (GBK); any non-GBK character makes json.dumps raise UnicodeEncodeError and the whole tools/call becomes -32603. Encoding applies to stdin too, otherwise Chinese arguments arrive as lone surrogates.
lessons.do: Read/write sys.stdin.buffer / sys.stdout.buffer with explicit utf-8, or reconfigure BOTH stdin and stdout/stderr.

lessons.scenario: Client mis-decodes tool results
lessons.trap: An HTTP response without an explicit charset lets the client guess a code page and garble non-ASCII payloads.
lessons.do: Always send Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8.

lessons.scenario: Calling the VBA6.DLL debug-engine exports to read the VB6 callstack
lessons.trap: Three separate mistakes all produce access violations that look like 'the API is unusable': (1) EbGetCallstackFunction arg5 is a POINTER (out long*), passing ByVal 0 writes to address 0; (2) frame indices are 0-BASED, so asking for frame == count walks past the list and reads [NULL+4]; (3) the out string is UTF-16 while the BSTR length is a byte count, so names come back with NULs between characters.
lessons.do: Declare arg5 ByRef Long, iterate frames 0..count-1 and clamp, and decode the name by taking every other character when NULs are present. EbGetCallstackCount only walks the list when EbMode()==2; otherwise it writes the sentinel 1.

lessons.scenario: VB6 add-in: a Declare-based helper (or any guarded code) ran just before you inspect Err
lessons.trap: Err is NOT cleared by a normal return, so reading Err.Number after a successful call can see a stale or phantom error (measured: a queued 17 KB response was aborted by a phantom error 5, and a GetLastError() probe read 0 instead of 87 because the Declare epilogue clobbered the thread last-error)
lessons.do: Never branch on Err after a normal return: only an error that ESCAPES the guarded call is a real failure. Wrap the call so its own handler reports that escaping error, clear or ignore Err unconditionally afterwards, and for Win32 last-error use Err.LastDllError (VB6 keeps it per-call) or a Toolhelp32 snapshot instead of a GetLastError() Declare.

lessons.scenario: Writing kernel32/user32 Declare statements in VB6 (e.g. named-pipe or Win32 transport code)
lessons.trap: A Declare without the Alias clause compiles fine and only fails at the FIRST CALL with run-time error 453 (cannot find the entry point in the DLL) - 17 occurrences in one card.
lessons.do: Always give the Alias form for kernel32/user32 functions and make the first use fail-loud (log event=start_failed err=453), otherwise the failure looks like "no transport is running at all".

lessons.scenario: A VB6 named-pipe server that writes a reply frame and then closes the pipe
lessons.trap: DisconnectNamedPipe discards frames already written into the buffer, so the client sees a bare EOF and the reply reason is lost.
lessons.do: After writing the frame, let the client read it (or wait a short grace period, e.g. 750 ms) and then CloseHandle; do not call DisconnectNamedPipe for this path. Also never call FlushFileBuffers if it can block until the client drains.

lessons.scenario: Passing a VB6 string to a Win32 API that expects an ANSI/byte buffer (e.g. a security descriptor)
lessons.trap: VB6 strings are UTF-16; copying ANSI bytes straight into StrPtr(s) corrupts the data - a SID became garbage, ConvertStringSecurityDescriptor returned ERROR_INVALID_SID (1337) and the ACL silently fell back to the default DACL.
lessons.do: Build a Byte() array and convert with StrConv in the documented direction; never assume StrPtr gives an ANSI buffer, and treat a silent ACL fallback as a bug, not a default.

lessons.scenario: Calling a pipe-transport MCP over more than one connection at a time.
lessons.trap: The pipe is defined with a single instance: a second concurrent connection is refused as busy (ERROR_PIPE_BUSY 231) and there is no TCP fallback, so the second call fails even though the service is healthy. Opening a parallel connection to read while a write is in flight cannot work.
lessons.do: Multiplex requests on ONE connection (the protocol already carries request ids) or serialise your calls. If you must observe progress during a long call, use the same connection.

lessons.scenario: Reaching the management tools by talking HTTP to the middle service.
lessons.trap: The management tools (list, target, start, stop, restart the IDE, plus the lesson tools) live on the hub face only; the HTTP face exposes the add-in tools. A client that speaks HTTP to the service simply does not have them.
lessons.do: Drive those tools through the hub (stdio). Check which face you are on before concluding a tool is missing.

lessons.scenario: Recovering a wedged IDE with the restart tool while the service or hub was started outside a desktop session.
lessons.trap: The restart path saves, asks the IDE to quit and force-kills it, then relaunches - but processes launched from a non-interactive context land in session 0, so no usable IDE appears and readiness waits out its budget while reporting only a refusal.
lessons.do: Run the service or hub inside the interactive session (user logon / interactive scheduled task). Supply the project path explicitly when the transport is a pipe, and treat a refusal as 'no usable IDE came back', not as 'nothing happened'.

lessons.scenario: Concluding that a long tool call produced no result because the console showed nothing.
lessons.trap: Long-running calls are usually driven detached and write their receipt to a file; an empty console is not evidence of a missing receipt. Declaring 'no result' when the receipt is on disk wastes a whole round and can hide a real answer.
lessons.do: Read the evidence file (and the service log) before concluding either way; state which file you read and what it contained.

lessons.scenario: Every static/lexical gate is green, yet the VB6 project will not compile
lessons.trap: Lexical and structural gates cannot prove compilability. In one batch a reserved word used as a Dim identifier (VB6 compares names case-insensitively, so reM IS Rem) and a single 1055-character source line (VB6's limit is 1023) both passed every static check; only the real /make refused the tree.
lessons.do: Treat a green gate set as NECESSARY, never sufficient: run a real build (offline /make or make_project) early in any batch that touches VB source, not as the last step, and keep a lexical gate over the .vbp component set for the two classes that actually stopped a build (reserved identifiers, lines over 1023 characters).
